summary: Import-time PATH hijack enables CWD-first binary resolution
details: On require(), index.js executes `process.env.PATH = '.';` at module top level, replacing the Node process's PATH environment variable with the current working directory for the remainder of the process lifetime. Any subsequent `child_process.exec`/`spawn` call that resolves a bare command name (e.g., `ls`, `git`, `node`, `sh`) will search the current working directory first, so a file placed in CWD with a common binary name will execute instead of the real system binary. The package is advertised as a parser/compression helper and has no documented need to mutate PATH. The mutation is unconditional, global to the installer process, and silent — providing a covert local code-execution primitive triggered by any downstream code that shells out by bare name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
